_comment: Hook-concern admission ledger. FORWARD-ONLY: the 55 concerns present at the time this file landed (2026-08-30) are grandfathered by construction — the gate's scope is the SET DIFFERENCE of concern ids between the base ref and HEAD, so a pre-existing concern can neither demand a row nor be forgotten off one. Every concern added from here on needs an `admitted` row answering all five questions, or check_concern_admissions fails.

The five answers are derived from docs/contracts/hook-architecture-v1.md, not from the skill ledger's questions: slot · binding_hosts · behaviour_where_deny_ignored · why_not_extend · per_event_budget_impact. What makes a concern risky is that it binds to a slot, on hosts that may or may not honour a deny, inside a per-event budget — and none of that has a skill analogue.

`decision: rejected` is FIRST-CLASS: a recorded refusal is the point, not an absence. A rejected row naming a concern that EXISTS is a hard failure — it means the refusal was overridden without updating its row, which is worse than no record at all.

binding_hosts: Bound on every host whose post_tool_use slot already carries edit-shape (augment, claude, cowork, cursor, cline, gemini). Only claude is verified to forward a warn verdict's additional_context to the model; elsewhere the advisory is emitted and the host's handling is unverified, which costs nothing because the concern cannot block anywhere.
behaviour_where_deny_ignored: Identical everywhere: this concern never denies. It reports severity advisory at EXIT_WARN, which host_semantics.emitFor reduces to exit 0 with the text in additionalContext. A host that discards dispatcher output loses the nudge and changes nothing else — the deterministic refusal lives in the lint_code_comments gate, not here.
why_not_extend: edit-shape is the only post_tool_use concern reading the same payload field, and its subject is diff ECONOMY (a whole-file Write for a small change). Folding a comment-content classifier into it would give one concern two unrelated fire conditions and one rollback switch for both. It also fires once per session by design, which is the exact cadence this concern must not have: the measured failure was 41 files each carrying the defect.
per_event_budget_impact: +1 on post_tool_use, taking that slot from 12 to 13 against DEFAULT_MAX_PER_EVENT=8 — a cap this slot already exceeds and which ships DEFAULT_HARD_FAIL=false. Runtime cost is one regex pass over the payload string already in memory: no fs read, no spawn, no git call, unlike edit-shape which spawns git diff. Stated rather than minimised: the slot is over its nominal budget and this addition does not fix that.
reason: The code clause of language-and-tone named check_md_language as its enforcer, and that validator rejects every non-.md path (check_md_language.ts:175) — an enforced_by entry that structurally cannot see a source file. code-comment-discipline carries no enforced_by at all and is type: auto on prompt keywords, so a run writing 45 files without the user typing comment/refactor/implement never loads it. Measured 2026-09-02 in a consumer repository: 509 German comment lines and 21 report- or provenance-shaped comments across 41 of 45 changed source files, including a 101-line colour-analysis report inside a CSS file.

binding_hosts: Bound on every host whose post_tool_use slot already carries pr-url-reminder (augment, claude, cowork, cursor, cline, gemini). Only claude is verified to forward a warn verdict's additional_context to the model; elsewhere the advisory is emitted and the host's handling is unverified. windsurf and copilot carry no post_tool_use slot at all, so there the settle obligation stays model-carried by the git-workflow skill alone — stated in the skill's reference rather than implied away.
behaviour_where_deny_ignored: Identical everywhere: this concern never denies. It reports severity advisory at EXIT_WARN, which host_semantics.emitFor reduces to exit 0 with the text in additionalContext. A host that discards dispatcher output loses the reminder and changes nothing else — there is no deterministic refusal behind it, and none is claimed.
why_not_extend: pr-url-reminder is the nearest neighbour and fires on a different event for a different purpose: it shapes the REPLY after a PR is created (the URL must be the literal last line), and it is silent on every push that does not create a PR — which is most of them, including every follow-up push to an open PR. Folding a push-settle branch into it would make one concern answer two unrelated questions on two disjoint trigger sets, and would inherit its gh-pr-create matcher, which is precisely the wrong trigger here. The trigger this concern needs is git's own ref-advance report, which pr-url-reminder never reads.
per_event_budget_impact: Zero on the overwhelming majority of post_tool_use events: the fire path requires git's ref-advance report in the tool output, so every non-push tool call exits after two regex tests on strings already in memory. On an actual push it adds one best-effort `gh pr view` (15 s timeout, failure swallowed) to resolve the PR number, so the reminder can carry the literal ci_settle command instead of a flag. Pushes are rare per session; the measured corpus behind this concern shows single-digit pushes per session against thousands of tool calls.
reason: Measured over the 30 sessions and 50 PRs preceding 2026-09-04: 22 of 30 sessions ran `gh run view --log-failed`, 17 of the 36 PRs whose workflow runs were still readable carried at least one failed run (56 runs), and 20 of 50 PRs carried a follow-up fix(ci|gates|budget) commit (41 commits). Every one of those pushes SUCCEEDED — what failed was the ending, where verify-before-complete is model-carried at exactly the moment a turn feels finished. The concern makes the push's own unfinishedness observable at the one point where it is a deterministic fact rather than a judgement.

binding_hosts: claude ONLY, and deliberately narrower than the slot's declared set. augment, cowork, cursor, cline and gemini all declare pre_tool_use, but claude is the one platform this repository has verified both binds the slot and acts on the dispatcher's verdict (hook-architecture-v1.md, Which hosts carry pre_tool_use). augment's and cowork's trampolines discard dispatcher output and exit 0 unconditionally, so a deny bound there would run and be ignored. `agent-config hooks:status` answers this for the host actually running, and it is the answer to prefer over this row.
behaviour_where_deny_ignored: It is not bound where the deny would be ignored, so there is no such host today — that is the whole reason for the narrow binding above. If it were later bound on a discarding host, the refusal would become a no-op and the constraint would fall back to prose: ask-when-uncertain's one-question-per-turn Iron Law and user-interaction's one-decision-point clause, which are always-loaded kernel rules and are the floor on every host regardless. Nothing else changes: the concern writes no state, reads no file and makes no network call.
why_not_extend: The four existing pre_tool_use refusals answer disjoint questions on disjoint payloads: block-no-verify classifies a git command string, block-kernel-rule-writes and block-speaking-inbox-dir classify a target PATH, block-config-weakening counts allowlist entries across a session. This one classifies the ARITY of a question payload on a tool none of them targets, and it is the only one whose subject is ask shape rather than a write. Folding it into any of them would give that concern two unrelated fire conditions, two payload readers and one rollback switch for both — and would inherit a tools: filter that is exactly wrong for it. evidence-independence is the nearest by subject (it also reads a prompt the agent is about to send) and is still the wrong home: it judges an evaluation prompt's neutrality, which shares no predicate with counting questions.
per_event_budget_impact: +1 on claude's pre_tool_use, taking that slot from 14 to 15 against DEFAULT_MAX_PER_EVENT=8 — a cap this slot already exceeds and which ships DEFAULT_HARD_FAIL=false. Stated rather than minimised: the slot is over its nominal budget and this addition does not fix that. The runtime cost is bounded far below the other entries, though, because the manifest's per-concern tools: filter means the dispatcher skips it in-process for every tool that is not a structured-ask candidate — which is every tool call on every host measured today. When it does run it is one JSON.parse of a payload already in memory plus one regex test: no fs read, no spawn, no git call.
reason: ask-when-uncertain's Iron Law is one question per turn and user-interaction narrows 'one' to one decision point answerable with a single reply. Both are kernel rules and both are model-carried at the ask surface: user-interaction.md records a 30-session conformance audit in which every malformed ask escaped the numbered-block surface that check_reply_consistency reads, and states plainly that no gate ships for that class. A host's native question picker makes the N-in-one violation cheap and structured, which is precisely the shape a deterministic check CAN see — a payload's question array has a length, where prose does not. The concern fires on nothing today (no host in the capability registry carries an observed structured-ask tool, per _lib/structured_ask.ts) and exists so the first host to ship a picker meets the rule already in force rather than after a measured regression. It denies rather than truncating to the first question: a truncation would hide exactly the decisions the user was owed, invisibly, at the moment they were asked for.

binding_hosts: Bound on all three platforms whose pre_tool_use list already carries code-graph-nudge (augment, claude, cowork). Only claude is verified to forward a warn verdict's additionalContext to the model; on augment and cowork the trampolines discard dispatcher output and exit 0, so the advisory is emitted and its delivery is unverified. That costs nothing here because the concern never denies — there is no refusal to be discarded. Hosts with no pre_tool_use binding carry the obligation through the rule text alone. `agent-config hooks:status` answers this for the host actually running and is the answer to prefer over this row.
behaviour_where_deny_ignored: Identical everywhere: this concern never denies. It reports severity advisory at EXIT_WARN, which host_semantics.emitFor reduces to exit 0 with the text in additionalContext, verified end-to-end through the dispatcher in both polarities. A host that discards dispatcher output loses one advisory line and changes nothing else. No deterministic refusal sits behind it and none is claimed: compliance with the rule stays model-carried on every host, including claude.
why_not_extend: The nearest neighbours read a different thing for a different purpose. rtk-wrap and ship-diff-volume both read a shell command string, but rtk-wrap decides output filtering and ship-diff-volume classifies a ship VERB against diff volume — neither has a predicate about command COMPOSITION, and folding this in would give one concern two unrelated fire conditions on overlapping payloads with one rollback switch for both. code-graph-nudge is the closest in shape (advisory, once per session, same slot) and is the wrong home by subject: it answers whether a code-graph should be queried before a read, which shares no predicate with whether a call chains work steps. rule-inject is the one concern that could have delivered this rule body instead, and it ships default-off behind lean_projection.mode: delivery and unbound on the default role, so it is not a carrier today.
per_event_budget_impact: +1 on the pre_tool_use slot of three platforms. Emission is 491 bytes, under the 1024-byte default_cap_bytes in hook-token-budget.json, so no per-concern row is registered. It fires at most ONCE per session (a latch keyed by session id under agents/runtime/state/), so its contribution to the 2048-byte per-slot sum is a one-time 491 bytes rather than a per-call cost. On every other call the work is one JSON.parse of a payload already in memory, a set membership test on the tool name, and a single-pass scan of the command string: no fs read outside the latch check, no spawn, no network.
reason: token-efficiency's One command per Bash call is a permission rule whose obligation applies at tool-call time, and its own triggers match the PROMPT — nothing in a prompt announces that the next call will be chained, so the rule was unreachable exactly when it mattered. The host splits a compound command on the shell operators and requires each segment to match the allowlist independently, so one unmatched segment sends the whole call down the permission path even when every other segment was allowed. Measured over 40,268 real Bash calls: 97.7% carry a shell metacharacter, 17.9% have a head token matching no allowlist pattern, and 5,037 of those are a leading VAR= assignment — a shape no allowlist pattern can express, so it shrinks only by not being written. The concern is the reach, and it is advisory because the alternative would be a shell parser with a security boundary attached.

binding_hosts: Bound on the same three platforms whose pre_tool_use list carried its predecessor code-graph-nudge, which this concern replaces one-for-one (verified: three pre_tool_use lists name it, and none names the old id). Only claude is verified to forward a warn verdict's additionalContext to the model; on augment and cowork the trampolines discard dispatcher output and exit 0, so the line is emitted and its delivery is unverified. Hosts with no pre_tool_use binding carry the same obligation through the rule text instead — external-code-graph-interop was condensed in this change and now points at code-intelligence for the per-host delivery detail. `agent-config hooks:status` answers this for the host actually running and is the answer to prefer over this row.
behaviour_where_deny_ignored: Identical everywhere: this concern never denies. severity advisory at EXIT_WARN, which host_semantics.emitFor reduces to exit 0 with the text in hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext on claude. A host that discards dispatcher output loses one state line and changes nothing else, and the hook's own header states that case explicitly. No deterministic refusal sits behind it and none is claimed.
why_not_extend: It IS the extension — of code-graph-nudge, which it replaces rather than joins, and the replacement is why a new id exists at all. Two behavioural changes make it not a rename: the nudge also fired on ABSENT, advertising a capability the consumer had not built and, before the parsers shipped, could not build; and it carried an instruction where this carries STATE (`fresh` / `behind:N`), which is a fact the model cannot otherwise see. Silent-on-absent is what makes default-on defensible. Folding it back into the nudge would mean keeping the advertisement.
per_event_budget_impact: Net ZERO on the pre_tool_use slot count: one concern replaces one concern on all three binding platforms. No per-concern row is registered in hook-token-budget.json (verified: the file carries no code_graph entry), so it sits under the 1024-byte default_cap_bytes. NOT independently measured in this change, and the figure is deliberately not asserted: the emission size belongs to the branch that authored the hook. A `tools:` filter restricts it to Grep / Glob / Read, pinned by a test against the hook's own branch surface, so it is skipped in-process on every other tool.
reason: The flag the predecessor shipped behind (hooks.code_graph.enabled) gated a nudge whose common case was 'you do not have this'. Phase 0.1 of road-to-a-graph-that-is-shipped made the parser install unnecessary, so the flag's premise was gone; the replacement speaks only when a graph exists and reports its staleness, which is the one thing that changes a decision — an answer from a graph N commits stale is worth less than the same answer from a fresh one, and only the hook knows N. This row was missing on arrival and is written here rather than left for the gate to keep reporting; every claim in it is transcribed from the hook's own header, the manifest, or a file read, and the one figure that would have needed a fresh measurement is declined above instead of invented.

binding_hosts: Bound on `claude` ALONE, which is narrower than the seven platforms whose session_start list it could have joined. The reason is the reader: `end-review-nudge` is bound on claude's stop slot and nowhere else, and cowork refuses it explicitly in the manifest. Binding the writer on the other six would spend two git subprocesses per session start to produce a file nothing opens. It is also dropped for the `worker` role beside its reader, for the same derived reason rather than a clause of its own. Where the baseline is absent the nudge reads `absent` and degrades to exactly its pre-change behaviour, recorded in its telemetry row rather than inferred. `agent-config hooks:status` answers this for the host actually running and is the answer to prefer over this row.
behaviour_where_deny_ignored: Identical everywhere: this concern never denies and emits no context. It is capture-only, always returns 0, and its entire output is one JSON file under `agents/runtime/state/review-baseline/`. A host that discards dispatcher output loses nothing, because there is nothing on stdout to discard. An unwritable state directory is caught and degrades the reader to `absent`; a session start is never failed by it. No deterministic refusal sits behind it and none is claimed.
why_not_extend: `session-register` is the closest neighbour — same slot, already writes per-session state, already prunes — and it is the wrong home by subject: it answers which sessions are live on this repository, and folding a git measurement into it would give one concern two unrelated fire conditions and one rollback switch for both. `end-review-nudge` itself cannot hold it: it runs on `stop`, and by its first stop the session has already mutated the tree the baseline is supposed to predate. That ordering is the whole mechanism, not an implementation detail. What IS shared rather than duplicated is the measurement: `totalNonDocMutatedLinesWithMeasure` and `deriveSessionKey` are imported from the nudge, so the two sides cannot drift on what a non-doc mutated line is or on how a session is keyed.
per_event_budget_impact: +1 on the session_start slot of ONE platform. Emission is zero bytes — the concern writes no stdout at all, so no per-concern row is registered in hook-token-budget.json and it cannot contribute to the per-slot sum. The cost is wall-clock rather than tokens, and it is stated rather than estimated: measured on this tree, `git rev-parse HEAD` 11-14 ms, `git diff --numstat HEAD` 22-29 ms, `git ls-files --others` 55-57 ms — about 91 ms, ONCE per session, behind an `existsSync` latch that makes a second session_start a no-op. On the reader's side the change is net-negative on two of three branches: `currentHeadSha` is now passed as a thunk, so the `absent` and `unreadable` paths — the steady state on every host without the nudge — no longer spawn a git process they would have discarded.
reason: `end_review_nudge_hook`'s own header recorded a measurement defect and the reason it was not fixed: pre-existing uncommitted changes are charged to the session, because 'no such baseline exists anywhere a `stop` concern can read it (recording one would be new session-wide state, out of this roadmap phase's one-concern scope)'. That reason went stale — session_start is bound on seven hosts carrying fourteen concerns — and the defect escalated: on an accumulator branch the nudge read 1,771 lines of two crashed sessions' uncommitted work and fired every turn. An advisory that always fires is noise, and noise is worse than silence because it trains the reader to skip the one that mattered. Three states make the subtraction invalid — no baseline, an unreadable one, a moved HEAD, and a mixed measure — and all of them fall back to the UNSUBTRACTED count rather than to silence, because a safety advisory must not be disarmed by its own instrumentation failing. Each fallback is carried into the `review_skipped` row as a closed enum, so the rate at which the mechanism degrades is measurable from its own stream rather than assumed. Honest limit, recorded here and at the mechanism: the baseline is written once and never refreshed, so from a session's first commit onward `head_moved` holds and the pre-existing tree is charged again. Re-baselining is not attempted because a second write cannot tell 'we committed our own work' from 'a peer session committed underneath us' from a stop payload.
